title: Sixth, Fifth, Third, Second — First: Neumann Never Headed on the Lisbon Coast
title_candidates: Sixth, Fifth, Third, Second — First: Neumann Never Headed on the Lisbon Coast
The Long Way Up: Two Spoons, Then a Trophy
Never Headed: Neumann's 156 on the Lisbon Coast
Estoril Rewrites Its Book at Both Ends
theme: A man who had only ever gone backwards or nearly-there finally arrives: Neumann leads from the first afternoon at Oitavos and is never headed, while the rest of the field spends four days handing the course its own material — two course-worst records, three double-figure holes and one genuine course record.
tone: house — faithful, entertaining, tongue-in-cheek British English; subverted gravitas, trivial stakes handled with the solemnity of statecraft
opening_hook: Open on the plain ledger of Stuart Neumann's TEG career — 6th, 5th, 3rd, 2nd, and two Wooden Spoons in the cupboard — then start at Oitavos Dunes on the Saturday, where he posted 39 and took a lead nobody would take off him.
foreshadow: Neumann's finishing ladder across the last four TEGs he played — 6th, 5th, 3rd, 2nd — and the two Spoons that sit behind it
Penha Longa's par-five 12th, SI 17 and nominally one of the easiest holes on the card, noted early as harmless
Alex Baker arrives as reigning Spoon holder (TEG 15) and opens with a 9 at the very first hole of the tournament
Gregg Williams arrives as defending Trophy champion and immediately posts the best gross in the field — 89, his best ever round at Oitavos

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.winner_or_loser: Alex Baker — 127 pts, 4 behind Jon Baker

headline_candidates: Neumann Opens With 39 and a Lead He Never Gives Back
Alex Baker Rewrites the Oitavos Ledger, Downwards
Atlantic Links, Arthur Hills, and a 10 at the 17th
rounds.chosen_headline: Neumann Opens With 39 and a Lead He Never Gives Back
rounds.angle: On the third TEG round at Oitavos Dunes, Neumann's 39 puts him five clear immediately; Williams answers with the best gross in the field, 89, his own personal best there; and at the other end Alex Baker signs for 113, a new course-worst across 12 prior visits.

headline_candidates: A New Course, the Same Two Leaders
Alex Baker Concedes the Bottom for Good at the 13th
rounds.chosen_headline: A New Course, the Same Two Leaders
rounds.angle: Troia is new to TEG so nobody has history to hide behind: Neumann's 35 is still best in the field and the lead goes to 7, Jon Baker draws level for the gross lead at the 11th and 14th — the closest the Jacket ever came — and Alex Baker bleeds 13 shots from the 13th and takes outright last in the Spoon race for keeps.

headline_candidates: Both Bakers Broken by the Same Par Five
The Sintra Hills Present Their Invoice
Neumann's Second 39 Turns a Contest Into Paperwork
rounds.chosen_headline: Both Bakers Broken by the Same Par Five
rounds.angle: At Penha Longa's 12th — SI 17, supposedly the soft spot — Jon Baker takes 10 and Alex Baker 9; Mullin loses an 8 at the 16th (SI 1) and slides to 30 points; Williams's five straight pars from the 11th push the Jacket lead from 4 to 14 while Neumann's 39 pushes the Trophy lead to 12.

headline_candidates: Estoril Rewrites Its Book at Both Ends
Two 80s and a 107 on Portugal's Oldest Card
rounds.chosen_headline: Estoril Rewrites Its Book at Both Ends
rounds.angle: Mullin's 80 is a new Estoril course record, beating 86 across 6 prior visits, and a 14-shot improvement on his last visit; Williams matches the number for his own Estoril best and closes the Jacket out at +66; Neumann posts his tournament-best 43 despite a 9 at the 8th (SI 1); Alex Baker's 107 is a new Estoril course-worst, complete with an 11 at the 12th.

players.arc: Two prior Wooden Spoons, no wins and a best-ever second: he led the Trophy from Oitavos to Estoril with 39-35-39-43, best in the field in the first three rounds, never worse than second of five, and closed with a 14-shot improvement on his last visit to Estoril.

The defending Trophy champion lost the crown while being the best gross player in the field in all four rounds — +66 for the Jacket, the fifth-best gross in TEG history, and yet beaten head-to-head by Neumann on every one of the four days.

Nine prior Jackets and a shrug of a Penha Longa (30 points, an 8 at the 16th, 13 shots worse than his last visit there) answered by 45 points and an 80 at Estoril — a new course record and a personal best by 14 — which still left him 16 adrift of Williams.

A personal best 92 at Oitavos to start, then 11 shots gone in three holes at Penha Longa including a 10 at the 12th; a new Estoril best of 93 to finish, and the small mercy of being 4 points clear of his brother.

The reigning Spoon holder retained it in comprehensive style: 9s at the 1st and 11th and a 10 at the 17th on day one, a new Oitavos course-worst of 113, a new Estoril course-worst of 107, an 11 at the 12th, and last place in the Trophy race from the opening hole to the last.

venue_notes: TEG's 5th visit to the Lisbon Coast, four courses in four days: Oitavos Dunes (3rd TEG round there; Arthur Hills links on the Atlantic, host of Portuguese Opens) as the exposed opener; Troia (a new course for TEG, Robert Trent Jones Sr. on the Setubal peninsula) in R2, where nobody has any history to lean on, so no personal-best talk is available; Penha Longa (3rd TEG round there; RTJ Jr. mountain parkland in the Sintra hills, steep and long-regarded as one of Portugal's hardest) as the day the field bled; and Estoril in R4 (2nd TEG round there; Portugal's first golf club, short, tree-lined, Mackenzie Ross), the friendliest card of the four — which is exactly where the course record fell at one end and the course-worst at the other.
course_history_notes: Mullin's 80 at Estoril in R4 was both a new personal best there (by 14) and a new course record, beating 86 across 6 prior visits.
Williams set personal bests at two venues: 89 at Oitavos Dunes in R1 (by 2) and 80 at Estoril in R4 (by 6).
Neumann's 92 at Estoril in R4 was a new personal best there — 14 shots better than his last visit.
Penha Longa punished the returners: Jon Baker 12 shots worse than his last visit, Mullin 13 worse, Neumann 6 worse; Alex Baker was 10 worse at Oitavos and 8 worse at Estoril.

trophy_storyline.subject: Stuart Neumann's first Trophy, built from the front
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: A player whose TEG record consisted of two Wooden Spoons and a best finish of second led every round of the tournament and won by 13 — the first win of his career.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: Neumann arrives with two prior Spoons and a runner-up finish at TEG 15 as his high-water mark, then posts 39 at Oitavos and is five clear before the sun has properly set. Turn: he is best in the field again at Troia and again at Penha Longa, beating Williams head-to-head all four days, and the lead ratchets 5 to 7 to 12 with no lead change after the opening exchanges. Resolution: 43 points at Estoril — his best of the tournament, and posted with a 9 at the 8th on the card — for 156 and a 13-point win that was never in doubt.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams's Green Jacket at +66
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Dethroned as Trophy champion, Williams was still the best gross player in the field in all four rounds and posted the fifth-best gross aggregate in TEG history.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: 89 at Oitavos, his best ever there, gives him a 3-shot gross lead, and Jon Baker's level-pegging at the 11th and 14th at Troia is the only moment it looks contestable. Turn: Penha Longa settles it — a triple at the 7th answered by five consecutive pars from the 11th, an 87 while Mullin goes 98 and Jon Baker 97, and the lead balloons from 4 to 14. Resolution: 80 at Estoril, his own personal best there, on the same afternoon Mullin's matching 80 broke the course record — +66 and a 16-shot Jacket.

spoon_storyline.subject: Alex Baker's back-to-back Wooden Spoon
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The reigning Spoon holder never left the bottom of the Trophy table for a single round and set new course-worst records at two different venues on the way.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: he opens the tournament with a 9 at the 1st at Oitavos, adds a 9 at the 11th and a 10 at the 17th, and signs for 113 — the worst gross ever recorded there across 12 prior visits. Turn: at Troia's 13th he drops to outright last in the Spoon race and stays there, having bled 13 shots over the closing five holes. Resolution: Penha Longa costs him 12 shots in four holes, and Estoril produces an 11 at the 12th and a 107 — a new course-worst there too — for 127 points and a second consecutive Spoon, 4 behind his brother.

discovered_storylines.subject: The twelfth hole
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Three of the tournament's biggest single-hole disasters happened at a 12th, including two in the same round on a par five rated SI 17 — nominally the softest hole on the card.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Penha Longa's 12th is a par five with a stroke index of 17, the sort of hole you are supposed to bank points on. Turn: in R3 it takes 10 from Jon Baker and 9 from Alex Baker inside the same afternoon, in both cases as the middle of a longer haemorrhage from the 11th. Resolution: a round later, on a different course, Estoril's 12th takes 11 from Alex Baker — a septuple bogey and his worst hole of the tournament.

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin's Penha Longa to Estoril reversal
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The holder of nine prior Jackets went from the worst round of his tournament to a course record inside 24 hours, and it still wasn't enough to win anything.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Penha Longa reduces him to 30 points and a gross 98 — 13 worse than his last visit — with an 8 at the 16th, SI 1, doing most of the damage. Turn: he steadies with two clean holes to close R3, then at Estoril birdies the 2nd, stops a bogey run with a birdie at the 7th and piles up 9 points from the 11th to the 13th. Resolution: 45 points and an 80 gross — a new Estoril course record, beating 86 across 6 prior visits, and a personal best there by 14 — which lifted him to Jacket runner-up, 16 behind.

payoffs.seed: Neumann's ladder: 6th, 5th, 3rd, 2nd, and two Spoons behind it

payoffs.payoff: 156 points, first place, wire-to-wire, by 13 — the top step reached at last, and his best round of the four was the final one (b01, b08).

payoffs.seed: Penha Longa's 12th, SI 17, described early as the soft spot
payoffs.payoff: Jon Baker 10 and Alex Baker 9 at that same par five in R3, and Alex Baker 11 at Estoril's 12th in R4 (b34, b44, b09).

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker arrives as reigning Spoon holder and opens with a 9 at the 1st
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 4 and the Wooden Spoon section
payoffs.payoff: Course-worst records at both Oitavos (113) and Estoril (107), an 11 at the 12th, and a second straight Spoon on 127 (cr03, cr02, b24).

payoffs.seed: Williams the defending Trophy champion, best gross in the field on day one
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 4 and 'How the three were decided'
payoffs.payoff: He kept the gross crown — +66, by 16, the fifth-best in TEG history — but was beaten head-to-head by Neumann on all four days and handed the Trophy over (b02, b01).

vehicle_fit_response.note: Alex Baker's inventory of blow-ups is genuinely spectacular and gets the whole Spoon section, but it's a subplot: the week is Neumann's climb from two Spoons to a first Trophy, and catalogue was the frame only three TEGs ago.

why_the_champion_won: He built it: best in the field in each of the first three rounds, never worse than 2nd of 5, beating Williams head-to-head on all four days — and Williams playing an ordinary round in place of his worst would still not have closed 13 points.
